title.narrative: Knowledge management, partnership, research and dialogue on gender, peace and security strengthened
Number of dialogue forums organised to increase synergy and dialogue on WPS Agenda between AU’s relevant organs, RECs and CSOs

actual.value: - Annual Forum on Women and Preventing/Countering Violent Extremism - Gender Forum: Magnifying the role of women in conflict prevention to silencing the guns in Africa - Hight level virtual forum: Women in Governance and Political Participation (WGPP): Enhancing African Women's role in leadership

A virtual forum for the launch of the 2020 report of the AUC chairperson on the status of women peace and security agenda in africa. Virtual African Union Peace and Security Council (PSC) Open Session on WPS in November 2021. The session was organised in collaboration with the PSC secretariat. The session brought on board (virtually) women in conflict zones to discuss and advocate with the PSC the impact of COVID-19 on the lives of women in conflict affected areas. • Virtual 2nd African forum on women peace and security organised in December 2021, which brought over 160 women participants from all regions of Africa.

GPSP-PAPS organised the 4th Africa Forum on WPS in December 2024. The AU Special Envoy on Women, Peace and Security organized a high-level conference in October 2023 to support Sudanese women’s advocacy and mobilization to end the war. Consultations with Africa First Ladies Peace Mission (AFLPM) to support women networks and national authority in implementing the WPS agenda. The consultation took place in March 2023. PAPS thought its GPSP and MDD organized a dialogue forum on sharing of experience on conflict prevention and early warning (EW) with Women Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) in December 2023

Third Africa Forum on Women Peace and Security (WPS), under the theme “Leveraging on WPS Monitoring to Enhance Women’s Participation and Leadership in Peace Processes in Africa” was organised in December 2022.

title.narrative: AU support to the development and adoption of National Action Plans (NAP’s) by member states enhanced

title.narrative: AU’ s capacity to enhance delivery by Member States on commitments on Women, peace and security strengthened
Number of Member States that report on the implementation of the WPS Agenda using the Continental Results Framework (CRF)

target.value: Institutionalised, regular and systematic monitoring and reporting on the implementation of the WPS agenda using the CRF.

actual.value: AU published in 2023 its 3rd Bi-annual Report on the implementation of the WPS Agenda in Africa which fosters accountability and is critical for monitoring. progress; the Regional Economic Communities/ Regional Mechanisms (RECs/RMs) and their Member States for their efforts in implementing the WPS agenda through the adoption of six (6) Regional Action Plans (RAPs) and thirty-five (35) National Action Plans (NAPs) on UNSCR 1325, making Africa the continent with the highest number of NAPs and RAPs. - Capacity building has led to an increased number of countries that submit their WPS country reports, generated using CRF to OSE.

title.narrative: Capacities of PSD staff to mainstream gender in all its divisions and Liaison offices reinforced
Development of concrete tools and mechanisms to improve PSD’s staff capability and capacity to integrate WPS Agenda % of PSD staff trained with an understanding of gender mainstreaming

target.value: 80% of PSD staff trained on gender mainstreaming tools

actual.value: - A training was organized with the objective to build the capacities of PAPS staff and ECOSOC cluster Chairs on Peace and Security as well as on Gender. Ensuring regular tracking and reporting on the implementation of the WPS policies and activities using common tools and parameters. 11 participants received training courses on the CRF. - Programme opted to collaborate with partners to develop online gender specialized courses which will be uploaded on the KMP dedicated to PAPS Gender mainstreaming and WPS. Tailored specialized course in Gender Mainstreaming Skills for conflict prevention and resolution at community level developed in collaboration with WANEP for the G5 Sahel Women’s Platform.

target.value: Formulate key operational Guidance Notes 45% of PSD staff trained on gender mainstreaming and gender analysis

actual.value: GPSP conducted a series of five online training courses on gender and WFP related issues (29/09/2020-26/11/2020): Gender Sensitive Conflict Regional and Global Women Peace and Security Normative Framework Gender Sensitive Early Warning Mechanism. Gender Mainstreaming in Mediation Gender Based-Violence.

target.value: 100% of staff trained on gender mainstreaming tools

actual.value: The Gender Peace and Security Programme developed a guideline with the specific purpose of providing support in how to mainstream gender, including to increase the capacity of D-PAPS staff to incorporate gender perspectives into their work. a curriculum training package on gender mainstreaming in SSR has been finalised. an expert meeting was organised to review and validate the operational guidance note (OGN) on gender mainstreaming in early warning mechanisms. training will be rolled before the end of 2024. The Political Affairs Peace and Security Department through its Gender Peace and Security Programme (GPSP) in collaboration with the African Union Mission for Mali and the Sahel (MISAHEL) organised a two-days specialized skills course on GBV.

target.value: New strategy formulated Systematic use of all operational Guidance Notes 60% of PSD staff trained on gender mainstreaming tools

actual.value: The draft strategy has been finalised

title.narrative: AU monitoring and reporting on the implementation of the WPS Agenda improved
Member States have reported against the Continental Results Framework and Number of PSC sessions that address WPS Agenda (2022-2023)

target.value: 4 PSC sessions that address WPS Agenda

actual.value: 2 PSC sessions. The two PSC sessions convened during the year were the 1063rd and 1109th sessions. The 1063rd meeting was an open session held at ministerial level with a specific focus on examining the nexus between urbanisation and the WPS agenda.The 1109th session was committed to the PSC’s annual commemoration of UNSC Resolution 1325 on WPS.

target.value: 23 Member States have reported against the CRF.

actual.value: 6 six member states had already submitted their reports. More countries have requested for extra time to enable them finalise report compilation and validation.

target.value: 16 Member States have reported against the Continental Results Framework

actual.value: The CRF reporting applies to member states and REC/REMs that have an action plan on WPS. For 2020 report (generated with data collected in 2019 and early 2020) twenty out of twenty-five countries that had adopted a national action plan by 2020 did submit country reports while four out of the six REC/REMS that have a regional plan did submit reports. Due to COVID-19, submission of reports in 2020 was not made.

target.value: 6 of PSC sessions that address WPS Agenda

actual.value: Two WPS sessions were held by the PSC in 2023. The first one of these was the 1144th session convened in March March. The second one was held in November, committed to the Commemoration of the UNSCR 1325 (2000) WPS.

title.narrative: AU’s capacity to efficiently integrate the WPS Agenda in all APSA components strengthened
Existence of relevant instruments and mechanisms to mainstream gender and Evidence-based advocacy, policy formulation and decisions

target.value: Existence of instruments to systematically integrate WPS into AU peace and security efforts Existence of mechanisms to promote synergies and data collection Existence of AUC instruments to integrate WPS into PCRD.

actual.value: The content and design layout of the PAPS Knowledge Management Platform (KMP) is prepared. When fully functional, the platform is expected to contribute to the development and management of knowledge on Gender and Women, Peace and Security in the continent. AU has a gender sensitive AU PCRD Policy framework.
